_note: Manual file for the R10 mechanism study (contract gtsio520-r10-private-review). class_overrides add to or change the derived classes in fidelity-classes.json; every entry needs a reason, and a part bound to a gate (it moves, meshes or is in the interference ledger) cannot be lowered. coverage_waivers accept a missing gate for ONE asset only (its SHA-256): when the asset changes the waiver no longer applies, so the gap must be closed by an audit or waived again on purpose. lesson_focus is the draft judgement (operate, identify or concept) that the lesson map uses; the instructor has not reviewed it. Guide: docs/fidelity-classes.md.

coverage_waivers.reason: The declared meshes (two in the timing and reduction train, seven in the accessory train) have no measured minimum clearance: the audit only measures meshes through a baked operating clip.
coverage_waivers.clears_when: an interference-audit.json for this asset lists every declared mesh in gear_meshes with ok true

1.note: History of mechanical engines: no R10 part is used.

2.note: History of aircraft engines: uses the Wright engine, not R10.

3.note: Terminologies: learners name cylinder, piston, crankshaft and dead centres on the model.

4.note: Thermodynamic cycles: learners relate the four strokes to crank and piston movement.

5.note: Classification: recognising cylinder arrangement from the model.

6.note: Cooling methods: locating fins, baffles and the air path.

7.note: Parts and construction: naming and locating the major structural and power parts.

8.note: Valve operating: following the motion from camshaft to valve.

9.note: Accessories and drives: tracing power paths and predicting rotation.

10.note: Power generation: following the push from burning gas to the propeller shaft.

11.note: Induction and exhaust: following the air and gas routes through the engine.

12.note: Performance calculations: arithmetic on the engine's figures.

13.note: Factors affecting power: explained from air and ignition, not from geometry.

14.note: Engine requirements: a summary of what an engine must deliver.

15.note: Operation malfunctions: causes and signs, named against parts but not simulated.

16.note: Maintenance and servicing: finding where a cylinder leaks and which parts an overhaul touches.

17.note: Light sport aircraft: regulation and selection, not geometry.

18.note: Practicals: observe, name and describe real parts on the lab engines.
